resources.string: Check the advanced setting, its range, and required credentials before connecting.
Two MASQUE hops use the selected HTTP transport. Leave empty for automatic endpoints; hops must use different IP addresses.
Helps HTTP/3 connect where the usual QUIC handshake is restricted. Leave enabled unless it causes connection problems.
Servers that find website addresses. Leave empty for the defaults. For custom servers, enter IP addresses separated by commas.

Enter a team name and either an enrollment token or both service token fields. Email sign-in needs an interactive terminal and is unavailable here. Secrets stay on this device and are omitted from settings backups.
One rule per line: example.com, full:example.com, keyword:ads, 10.0.0.0/8, cidr:fd00::/8, port:25, or private. Block takes priority. Domain rules require visible DNS names, SNI, or HTTP Host.
Matching traffic leaves the tunnel directly. These Core rules apply only to traffic routed through Aethon; Android app exclusions take effect first.
Optional in Device VPN mode, for example 127.0.0.1:1820. Use a different port from SOCKS and Tor. Proxy mode uses HTTP 127.0.0.1:1818 without changing this saved value.

Starts a separate Tor SOCKS5 proxy at 127.0.0.1:1821 for compatible apps. Set that address in the app you want to use with Tor. It does not route all Device VPN traffic through Tor. Connected requires verified HTTPS traffic through both the tunnel and Tor; bridges are not included.
Settings backups exclude organization credentials and upstream proxy URLs. Enter these again after restoring.
Gool over MASQUE carries a WireGuard WARP identity inside a MASQUE tunnel for a foreign exit; Classic Gool is the legacy WARP-in-WARP.
Gool over MASQUE only. Leave empty to use the endpoint its registration names. Format: 162.159.192.1:2408
Reach the key API only through the fragmented route, for networks that filter its domain. MASQUE-family protocols only.
ECH Auto only. udp://1.1.1.1, tcp://IP[:port], or an https:// resolver; @address= and @sni= may follow. Empty uses the default.
ECH Auto only. The domain whose key the lookup takes. Empty uses the default.
Colon-separated, BoringSSL names. Empty uses the built-in Chrome list. An invalid value stops the connection with the option named. HTTP/3 ignores this field.
Ordered colon-separated list; the first gets the key share. Empty uses the default. An invalid value stops the connection with the option named.
Adds random-looking filler values Chrome also sends, making the fingerprint less recognizable. On by default; turn off only for compatibility testing.
Verifies MASQUE gateways against the built-in Cloudflare certificate pins instead of accepting any certificate. This is pin-based checking, not standard authority validation.
Where key registration calls go. Empty uses the default service. An IP works with the firewall-mark routing the Core uses; the server name stays unchanged.
When Cloudflare refuses the saved identity, register a fresh one automatically. On by default; off keeps the saved identity even if it stops working.
Auto matches the Core\'s own resource detection. Low suits constrained devices, High uses more resources for throughput.
Diagnostic only: logs how much went up and down and how long the tunnel has been up, once a minute, in the connection log. The on-screen counters are measured separately and stay authoritative.
How long a connection through the tunnel may take to open. Default 30; raise on very slow networks.
HTTP/2 carrier only. How often a keepalive is sent. Default 15.
HTTP/2 carrier only. How long a keepalive may go unanswered. Default 20.
WireGuard-family only. How long an endpoint that failed twice stays out of rescans. Default 300.
WireGuard-family only. Silence before a tunnel counts as dead. Default 10.
Exit-country policy only. How often the exit is rechecked while connected; a tunnel that moves is replaced. Default 60.
Fragmentation only. Splits the ClientHello inside the server name instead of at a random offset. Off by default.
